LESSON: TAQWA (GOD CONSCIOUSNESS)

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Pillars of Iman
Topic 3.2: Taqwa (God Consciousness)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Taqwa (God Consciousness), part of Pillars of Iman in Grade 6 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: What actions lead to piety? 2. Why is taqwa important in the life of a Muslim?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read verses (Q. 2: 2-5, 3:133-135) from the Qur’an/digital devices /mus’haf and list down the qualities of mutaqiin,

2. match and sort the qualities of a pious person using flash cards,

3. search online/from a mus’haf/ verse (Q.2:43: 76, 7:96, 9:119, 19:72,) on taqwa and draw their significance,

4. keep a weekly log/diary on the activities that demonstrate taqwa. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read verses (Q. 2: 2-5, 3:133-135) from the Qur’an/digital devices /mus’haf and list down the qualities of mutaqiin,
2. match and sort the qualities of a pious person using flash cards,
3. search online/from a mus’haf/ verse (Q.2:43: 76, 7:96, 9:119, 19:72,) on taqwa and draw their significance,
4. keep a weekly log/diary on the activities that demonstrate taqwa. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Taqwa (God Consciousness) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: interacting with digital technology as learners search online verses (Q.2:43: 76, 7:96, 9:119, 19:72,) on

taqwa and draw their significance.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: researching skills as learners draw the significance of taqwa from the given verses

of the Qur’an

Values:
• Responsibility: accountability as learners demonstrate consciousness of Allah (S.W.T.).

• Integrity: accountability as learners maintain their fidelity to Allah (S.W.T.) by doing what is right.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills: responsibility as learners find information on the significance of taqwa.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Social Studies: has some aspect of integrity which is related to God consciousness.
